title: Wöhler's Urea and the End of Vital Force
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
objective: Chemists once believed only living things could make organic compounds. In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler heated an inorganic salt and made urea.

fill.q: Wöhler made urea in the year ____.
The idea that only living things make organic compounds was the ____ force theory.

tf.q: Ammonium cyanate is an inorganic salt.
tf.explain: That is why the result was so striking.

tf.q: Berzelius supported the vital force theory.
tf.explain: He held that life was needed.

tf.q: Urea and ammonium cyanate have different atoms.
tf.explain: They have the same atoms in a new arrangement.

tf.q: The vital force idea ended in a single day.

ar.a: Wöhler's experiment challenged the vital force theory.
ar.r: He made an organic compound from an inorganic salt.

ar.a: Urea and ammonium cyanate have the same formula CH₄N₂O.
ar.r: The same atoms are arranged differently.

mcq.explain: Two NH₂ groups on a C=O.
